name: Shaped Reverb
description: A reverb whose level follows a drawn shape instead of dying away: it can hold and stop dead, rise backwards into a cut, swell and fade, fall in a straight line or breathe in waves.

params.name: Shape
params.description: The outline the reverb's level follows. Gate holds steady and stops dead. Reverse grows louder and cuts off. Bloom swells in and fades away. Fall drops in a straight line. Pulse breathes in three waves.

params.name: Time
params.description: How long the shape lasts, from the note to its end. Short settings are a burst behind the note; long ones are a slow cloud. With Repeat up it is also the gap between repeats.

params.name: Density
params.description: How many reflections make up the shape and how blurred they are. Low settings are a handful of separate echoes; high settings are a smooth wash.

params.name: Pre-delay
params.description: A gap of silence between the note and the start of the shape, which keeps the note clear of the reverb.

params.name: Colour
params.description: Changes the tone along the shape. Below the centre the reverb gets darker as it goes on; above the centre it starts dark and opens up towards the end.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Takes the top off the whole reverb, and makes the tail lose its brightness sooner as it fades. Lower settings are darker and sit further back.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Takes the bottom out of the reverb so low notes do not turn to mud. Higher settings are thinner and lighter.

params.name: Modulation
params.description: Slow movement inside the reverb. A little keeps held notes from sounding fixed; more adds a gentle detuned shimmer.

params.name: Repeat
params.description: Plays the whole shape again and again, each pass quieter, darker and more blurred. High settings pulse for a long time.

params.name: Tail
params.description: Adds an ordinary fading reverb behind the shape, so its end is not dead silence. Higher settings are louder and ring for longer; at zero the shape ends in nothing.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the reverb spreads between the speakers. At zero it is mono; fully up the two sides are unrelated.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the reverb. Fully up is the reverb alone.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Models in outline the gated and reverse programs of early digital reverberators and their descendants, not any one unit: a diffused signal is read from a long delay line by sparse taps at pseudo-random positions with random signs, and the tap gains follow the chosen shape. The sparse tap layout is after the approach of Karjalainen and Järveläinen, "Reverberation Modeling Using Velvet Noise", and of Välimäki, Holm-Rasmussen, Alary and Lehtonen, "Late Reverberation Synthesis Using Filtered Velvet Noise"; no constants or details were taken from either. The diffuser is a series of Schroeder allpasses whose moving lengths are read through first-order allpass interpolators; the tail is an eight-line feedback delay network with a Hadamard matrix, four of whose lines drift slowly.
